# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

I read the code directly. My shell access was denied, so I used file reads only. That was enough for every rule below.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

This is a small Next.js App Router site with four routes: `/`, `/varieties`, `/visit` and `/account`. The code gives no sign of a problem on any rule. These results are read from code, not measured on a running site. What code can't show is whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. That isn't scored.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing in the code needs fixing. The biggest open question is the one code can't answer.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your hosting or CDN
- **Why it matters:** your `robots.txt` welcomes search crawlers, but a firewall or CDN in front of the site could still block them.
- **Where:** outside the repository
- **What the code says:** `public/robots.txt:2` `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** stays 100. This check isn't scored, so it can't change the number.

To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`. It compares your access logs against the addresses crawlers publish.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain, 11 lines, valid directives |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Policy is `allow` for AI search. Only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` are blocked (lines 5-9), which matches `trainingCrawlers: block` |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes are indexable. `/account` is noindex but isn't in the sitemap or the nav |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes. Each is on `https://www.orchard.example`, e.g. `app/page.tsx:1` |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes are plain Server Components with static text |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No `application/ld+json` found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid. `public/robots.txt:11` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 indexable routes have both. `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"` |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable by server-rendered links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses plain `<a href>` to all three routes |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions that conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | No page-wide `nosnippet`, and no middleware or `headers()` found. `app/layout.tsx:9` uses element-level `data-nosnippet`, which is fine |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Read `app/layout.tsx` and the three pages. There are no images or unnamed controls |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app profile is declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` exists. That is fine and isn't counted |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app |

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server responses:** the real status for `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml`, redirects, and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside the repo. These are live-only checks. They don't change the code results.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- I left `/account` out of the scored routes. It is deliberately noindex and disallowed in `robots.txt`, so its missing description (`app/account/page.tsx:1`) is intentional.
- `public/` files are served at the site root, as Next.js does by default.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you want changes. None are needed right now.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
